reply_text:
㊣ ("work on our tasks and ping claude-16 when we need something") Agreed. I'll ping claude-16 only when -40° needs something from the 象 side, and you can jump between the two REPLs. On with crystallisation.

Design, building on what exists rather than adding new machinery:
- **In the hook (classical, milliseconds):** run `entities.py`'s existing rules on the changed memory, write its entity mentions, and append the memory to a queue.
- **In a bg.py worker (model tier, only for memory writes):** drain the queue. For each memory, run the existing Haiku entity pass on it, find its candidate pairs with `candidates.py`, and judge them with `judge.py`. Mentions are written directly; judged rows go through the existing `minus40.sorries load`.I'll pull two small pieces out of `entities.py` so the hook and worker can reuse them: the per-memory Haiku call, and the entity-id rule. Then the crystallise module:Wiring the classical tier into the hook. It runs only when a memory actually changed, inside the existing try, so it can never fail a tool call:The grep ran inside the same command, before the PostToolUse hook fired, so it couldn't see the new entry yet. Checking now:㊣ ("work on our tasks and ping claude-16 when we need something") Agreed and noted in my minus40 memory: claude-16 owns M-象-2000, and I'll ping it for 象-side needs.

㊥ (step 3, crystallisation) Done and live. A memory now picks up its structure as it's written: entities immediately, and a conflict check within about 30 seconds, so a new contradiction shows up as a sorry without anyone running a batch.

㊢ (how it works) It reuses the existing scripts rather than adding new machinery.
- **In the ingest hook, about 0.3 s, only when a memory changed:** the classical entity rules run on that memory, its mentions are written, and it's queued.
- **A bg.py worker, `minus40-crystallise`, only for queued memory writes, never turns:**
  1. Haiku extracts the memory's entities;
  2. the memory's candidate pairs are found and judged;
  3. findings go through the existing `minus40.sorries load`.

㊬ (checked)
- **A planted contradiction** in a throwaway test project (one memory says port 7777, the other 7778) became an open sorry with both quotes about 20 s after the write. I discharged that test sorry; you still have 18.
- **A real memory edit** (my own minus40 note) went through the live path: 8 rule mentions in the hook, then 15 Haiku mentions and 2 pairs judged unrelated by the worker, within 30 s.

㊩ (a bug the live check caught) The first real edit logged `No module named 'crystallise'`. The hook runs under `python3 -I`, which leaves the script's own folder off the import path. It's fixed, re-tested through the hook and the worker, and committed as `446c6bb`. The feature itself is `0e06dd2`.

㊟ (one limit) If you edit a memory and the edit resolves a conflict, the sorry isn't closed automatically yet; that still takes a discharge.

㊢ (what's running now, all on the scratch store, all under bg.py)
| job | what it does |
|---|---|
| scratch futon1b | the store, on :7093 |
| `minus40-follower` | turns, acts and ports; rewrites the inbox page |
| `minus40-faults` | errors and warnings |
| `minus40-crystallise` | the model tier for memory writes |
| ingest hook | in every Claude session |

The inbox is `~/code/data/minus40/open.html`.

🈰 (next) Step 5, the claude-14 replay. Its measures need ports we can trust, and that depends on claude-16 backfilling the missing reply text. So either I start now with the measures that don't depend on ports (memory versions written in the session and whether any entered a sorry; what the classical tier can read; faults in that window), or we wait for claude-16's backfill and do it all at once. My lean is to start now, without ports.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: ("weave them together") In Elephant-2000 terms the fit is direct. A warning is an assertion made by a component, an inbox item is the obligation it creates on someone, and discharging the item is meeting the obligation. That's the same open/closed shape as an operator's ask in 象, so one kernel could compute "open" across operator asks, agent bells and system faults alike. Running FUTON in a debugger then means faults become acts with owners. That's a design point to settle with claude-16 once it has said yes or no: whether faults enter M-象-2000's act vocabulary, or stay in -40° and only share the lifecycle.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text:
(its findings)
1. **No replies on the records.** For those turns, ports were computed from your fragments alone, so every opening fragment stayed open. The linking code was never even reached.
2. **Where replies exist, brackets are labels, not quotes.** Out of 797 marked paragraphs since 10-01, 662 carry labels like "where we are". Only 123 quote your words, and of those, 108 link correctly. The matcher works; the proforma practice mostly doesn't feed it.
3. **The replies are recoverable.** They're on :7073 as agent-chat evidence, chained to your turns, so they can be backfilled and the ports recomputed.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: ("almost nothing closed") My Checkpoint said the replies quoted your words and still nothing closed. That was wrong on both counts: there were no replies on the records, and 15 of my 17 brackets were labels. I've corrected my paragraph and the test-case file, attributing the correction to claude-16's finding (futon3c `58d9c0a1`, my text only). It's also a lesson for my own replies: when a paragraph answers something you said, quote your words, as the proforma asks. I'm doing that from now on.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text:
(its plan)
1. A lab note with the census script.
2. Discovery: does the reply evidence map one-to-one onto turn records? No writes.
3. If it does, backfill `reply_text` and recompute ports, then re-label the 24-row test case.
4. Only then propose how label-brackets should link, using numbers: a word-overlap match, or a "sole open port" rule, both recorded as inferences. It notes that `answers-inferred` exists in the kernel but is never populated on the live path.
5. Treat `constrain` as a standing rule rather than an open port, in the same class as grants and withdrawals.
